name: Bairro Alto Hotel
positioning: Boutique hotel in an 18th-century building on Praca Luis de Camoes, between Chiado and Bairro Alto in Lisbon's historic center
best_for: Travelers who want to stay between Chiado and Bairro Alto
Guests who value Portuguese art, design and cuisine

facts.text: The hotel is in Lisbon's historic center, between Chiado and Bairro Alto.
Praca Luis de Camoes is visible from the hotel's entrance.
The hotel reopened in 2019 after a three-year renovation.
Rooms have soundproofed windows that block out the noise of passing trams.
The ground-floor Patisserie makes Portuguese sweet and savoury pastries in the hotel throughout the day.
The Mezzanine bar on the ground floor serves healthy meals throughout the day.
The hotel's terrace has a view over the city and the Tejo river.
The wellness center has a Susanne Kaufmann spa and a gym.
The hotel is a member of The Leading Hotels of the World.
The hotel offers guests a guide to Lisbon with off-radar suggestions.
Tram 28 passes through Chiado near the hotel.

highlights.text: The hotel is housed in an 18th-century building with a primrose yellow exterior on Praca Luis de Camoes.
A sixth-floor bar is reserved for hotel residents, with views over the rooftops to the River Tagus.
The fifth-floor restaurant serves Portuguese cuisine created by Chef Bruno Rocha.
The hotel spans four Pombal-era buildings, so no two rooms are the same.
The interiors include specially commissioned pieces by Portuguese artists such as Vasco Araujo and Rui Chafes.

considerations.text: It is a steep walk down the hill to the banks of the River Tagus.
Conde Nast Traveler notes there are no especially child-friendly corners.
WhataHotel notes the hotel is in a lively nightlife district with evening noise.
